rationale.conceptual: The method relies on well-established plane-wave DFT (LDA, Car-Parrinello relaxations) but requires careful implementation of pseudopotentials (norm-conserving Si/Al, Vanderbilt ultrasoft O), uniform charge compensation for Al substitution, and consistent energy referencing for proton affinities/substitution energies. The physics is standard but demands accurate handling of several components.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves 12 separate geometry optimizations (all-silica, two Al substitutions, seven protonated configurations) across three structural scenarios, plus atomic reference calculations. It requires setting up a DFT code (Quantum ESPRESSO or similar), obtaining specific pseudopotentials, parsing multi-format output, and computing derived quantities. Orchestrating this sequence reliably is non-trivial.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires a series of periodic LDA plane-wave DFT calculations on a 54-atom zeolite cell using specific pseudopotentials and cutoffs from a 1994 paper. The method is conceptually a standard application of plane-wave DFT with some subtleties in pseudopotential selection and energy referencing (conceptual 3). The execution entails a multi-stage pipeline with many relaxations, DFT tooling setup, pseudopotential sourcing, and careful data extraction (execution 4). Resource needs are modest (small cell, CPU-only, <5 GB RAM).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The system is a small periodic cell (54 atoms), plane-wave cutoff 16 Ry, leading to ~8444 basis functions per orbital. Modern CPUs can handle such calculations in minutes to hours; GPU acceleration is unnecessary. Memory requirement is low (<4 GB). Input data is just the published crystal structure (few KB).
